sources.name: Labor Market AI Exposure: What Do We Know?
sources.authors: Gimbel, Kendall, Kulsakdinun — The Budget Lab at Yale

methodology.source_metric: Yale Budget Lab PCA-weighted consensus score (raw, not z-standardized)
methodology.mapping: TBL's PCA-weighted score aggregates six AI exposure metrics crosswalked to SOC 2018: Eloundou et al. dv_rating_beta and human_rating_beta (GPT-4 and human annotated task exposure), Eisfeldt et al. GenAI total and core (O*NET task productivity scoring), Felten et al. AIOE (MTurk survey of AI application abilities), and Tomlinson/Microsoft AI applicability score (Bing Copilot conversation analysis). Webb Pct AI excluded per TBL methodology (low PCA weight; captures distinct construct). The raw PCA score is mapped to JobOrBot's 1–9 replaceability scale using percentile bands on TBL's 777-occupation distribution (mean≈0, std≈2.16, range -3.4 to +7.1). Capped at 9 (not 10): TBL measures task overlap and exposure, not end-to-end job replacement. Multi-SOC OOH titles mapped by averaging PCA scores across constituent detailed SOC codes.
methodology.note: TBL key finding: metrics agree strongly on low-exposure occupations but diverge significantly on high-exposure ones. Cross-metric variance is reported in each rationale — treat scores ≥7 as directional signals, not precise estimates. 777/867 occupations have full 6-metric coverage.

target_scale.name: JobOrBot replaceability scale
target_scale.question: How close is AI to being able to do the whole occupation today?

anchors.meaning: AI is barely useful for doing the real job today.
AI is materially useful across substantial parts, but far from replacing it.
Strong multi-metric consensus that AI can handle the majority of this work today.
